core_obligations: Show that for X to Y to Z morphisms locally of finite type over S, families alpha of r-cycles on fibres of X/Y and beta of s-cycles on fibres of Y/Z, and gamma in Z_e(Z), one has (alpha composed beta) cap gamma = alpha cap (beta cap gamma) in Z_{r+s+e}(X) (proof lines 2934-2977). First, since the equality is of cycles on X, work locally on Z using lemma-action-opens (tag 0H67) and assume Z affine; then gamma is a finite combination of prime cycles and by lemma-action-bilinear (tag 0H66) it suffices to treat gamma = [W] for an integral closed subscheme W of delta-dimension e (proof lines 2935-2941). Second, for z the generic point of W write beta_z = sum m_j [V_j] in the cycle group of the fibre Y_z; then beta cap gamma = sum m_j [V-bar_j] with V-bar_j the integral closed subscheme of Y mapped into W with generic fibre V_j; at the generic points y_j of the V_j write alpha_{y_j} = sum n_{jk} [W_{jk}], so alpha cap (beta cap gamma) = sum m_j n_{jk} [W-bar_{jk}] where W-bar_{jk} is the integral closed subscheme of X mapped into V-bar_j with generic fibre W_{jk} (proof lines 2943-2956). Third, compute the composed family at z: (alpha composed beta)_z = (Y_z to Y)^*alpha cap beta_z = (Y_z to Y)^*alpha cap (sum m_j [V_j]) which by the construction of the cap product equals the cycle sum m_j n_{jk} [(W-bar_{jk})_z] on X_z; capping with [W] gives (alpha composed beta) cap [W] = sum m_j n_{jk} [W-tilde_{jk}] where W-tilde_{jk} is an integral closed subscheme of X mapped into W with generic fibre (W-bar_{jk})_z; since an integral closed subscheme of X mapping into W is determined by its generic fibre over z, W-tilde_{jk} = W-bar_{jk} and the two expansions agree (proof lines 2958-2976).
proof_roadmap: Localize on Z and reduce the test cycle to a prime cycle by bilinearity (proof lines 2935-2941).
Expand the cap-then-composition order: two-step unfolding at the generic points produces the cycle sum with closures W-bar_{jk} (proof lines 2943-2956).

Expand the composition-then-cap order: the composed family at the generic point is the cap of the pullback with the generic part, and capping with the prime cycle yields the same sum, the integral subschemes being determined by their generic fibres (proof lines 2958-2976).
